verdict_reason: The switch to code and Latin-name gates is correct, but the new species parameter is vaguely named, PERMANENT_ADDRESS has literal copies in check-answers, and a single-use literal sits at module scope.

todos.issue: permanentAddressApplies(species) names its parameter 'species', but every caller passes entry.speciesLatinName (card/view-model.js:107, form/forms.js:49) and the obligation gate reads speciesLatinName; under the old model 'species' held a species id, so the name no longer says which species value it takes
todos.fix: Must: the parameter is named for what it holds, the species Latin name, matching speciesLatinName used by the entry and the obligation gate. One way: rename to speciesLatinName.

todos.issue: PERMANENT_ADDRESS is now exported from fields.js as the permanent-address identifier id, yet check-answers/view-model/cards/consignment/species/identifier-columns.js:20-21 (changed in this PR) and identifier-cell.js:4 still spell 'permanentAddress' as a literal; the obligation manifest also names it (obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:166)
todos.fix: Must: one constant owns the permanent-address identifier id and every reader of it (identification table, check-answers columns and cell) uses that owner. One way: import PERMANENT_ADDRESS (or the obligation's name) in identifier-columns.js and identifier-cell.js in place of the literal.

todos.issue: IDENTIFIER_MAX_LENGTH = 58 is a literal held at module scope but used only by identifierChecksFor (line 30); the house rule puts a literal used by one function inside that function
todos.fix: Must: the 58-character limit lives inside identifierChecksFor, or is exported because another module or a test reads it. One way: move the constant into the identifierChecksFor body.
